correctness.rationale: With B=C[y,z], the two conics give a smooth integral Laurent polynomial ring R, free of rank four over B. Writing C=y²+z²−2y²z² gives x²=C+2yzst. The basis coefficient matrix for 1,x,x²,x³ in 1,s,t,st has determinant 4y²z²(y²−z²), proving that the displayed monic quartic is minimal over Frac(B). Hence A is its monogenic B-order, with the same fraction field as R; R is finite by the monic s,t equations and normal by smoothness. For an independent conductor check, write M^∨ for the B-trace dual in this fraction field. The monogenic identity A^∨=F_x(x)⁻¹A follows by Lagrange interpolation: Tr(h(x)/F_x(x)) is the coefficient of x³ in the remainder of h modulo F, and the coefficient pairing on 1,x,x²,x³ is unimodular (unit antidiagonal and zeros before it). The two quadratic sign involutions similarly give R^∨=(4st)⁻¹R, with dual basis 1/4,1/(4s),1/(4t),1/(4st). Biduality shows that rR⊂A iff rA^∨⊂R^∨; since A⊂R and 1∈A this is exactly r∈F_x(x)R^∨. Now F_x(x)=4x(x²−C)=8xyzst, giving (xyz)R. Multiplying 2xyz by the basis of R recovers the four claimed generators in A. Away from the image of xyz=0 the normalization is an isomorphism, and the equation on each coordinate plane cuts out the stated two lines set-theoretically. To check all other points, not just generic ones, symmetry reduces to (x,y,z)=(z₀,0,z₀), z₀≠0. Choose s=√(1−y²) near y=0 with s=1 there. In that neighborhood F factors as the product of (x−zs)²−y²(1−z²) and (x+zs)²−y²(1−z²); the second factor is a unit. If z₀²≠1 the first factors into two independent smooth linear coordinates in x−zs and y using a nonvanishing analytic square root of 1−z². If z₀²=1, c=1−z² is a local coordinate and the first factor is exactly a²−b²c with a=x−zs and b=y. Symmetry yields the twelve distinct points. Near the origin both analytic square roots exist; x=±z√(1−y²)±y√(1−z²) gives four smooth graphs with the four distinct tangent planes. This independently checks all strata over C; the supplied symbolic script was inspected and not executed.

evidence: The sine-addition parametrization and the polynomial in those examples are the same surface. In trace coordinates put U=y+is, V=z+it, W=i/(UV). Then UVW=i and the three traces (W+W⁻¹)/2, (U+U⁻¹)/2, (V+V⁻¹)/2 are respectively x,y,z. Thus (p_1,p_2,p_3)=(1,1,1), λ=i, c=(λ+λ⁻¹)/2=0 in the cited trace conventions.

value.rationale: This is a standard small nonnormal example from the triangle Lissajous/Kuramoto setting, not an arbitrary specialization: at this phase all six singular lines meet at a single four-branch point. The exact conductor gives scheme-level gluing data beyond the known support and separates it from the Jacobian scheme. The exhaustive analytic description distinguishes pinching from transverse double crossing and the four-branch origin. These are useful geometric invariants within the stated affine scope; no claim is made about infinity or an entire family.
